## Highlights
ChillMac 2.0 is a full redesign. The popover now leads with how your Mac is doing, keeps the numbers to one compact list, and replaces the old Performance Mode and per-fan switches with a single Cooling control. Your settings carry over: if Performance Mode was on, you're now on Smart cooling at the same intensity.
This update includes a new fan control helper, so macOS will ask you to allow ChillMac again in System Settings › General › Login Items & Extensions. Monitoring keeps working in the meantime, and later updates go back to one click.
## Fixed
- **Manual fan control on newer Macs.** On some Apple Silicon Macs, including the M4 Max, macOS took a moment to hand over the fans, ChillMac gave up too early, and the fans quietly stayed on automatic. ChillMac now waits for the handover, and if macOS still keeps control, the Cooling card says so.
## Added
- **One Cooling control.** Choose Automatic (macOS runs the fans), Smart (fans follow temperature) or Manual (you set each fan's speed). Smart's levels are now called Quiet, Balanced, Cool and Max. - **A welcome for new installs.** A short setup window explains the fan control helper before asking for it, then walks through cooling and menu bar options. Reopen it anytime from Settings. - **New app icon.** The snowflake is replaced by a fan, which also appears in the menu bar.
## Improvements
- **Easier-to-read panels.** Memory, Battery, Temperatures, CPU and Disk each open with a plain-language summary, and temperature sensors are grouped so you can expand only the ones you care about. - **Simpler Settings.** Fewer sections, clearer wording, and a place to reinstall or remove the fan control helper. - **Friendlier fan control setup.** Without the helper, ChillMac now explains what it does and what it never touches, instead of showing a warning. Monitoring works either way.

## Highlights
ChillMac now tells you when a new version is out without interrupting you. A small download badge appears on the menu bar fan, and opening ChillMac shows an Update button right at the top, no trip to Settings needed.
## Added
- **Update badge in the menu bar.** ChillMac checks for new versions every few hours in the background. When one is found, the fan icon gets a small download arrow in its corner. Choosing "Skip This Version" clears it - **Update button on the main screen.** A card at the top of the popover names the new version and installs it in one click. ChillMac relaunches itself when it's done - **Install with Homebrew.** `brew install --cask idevtim/tap/chillmac` now works, and Homebrew installs keep updating themselves like any other copy

## Highlights
Two things you can now switch on: the current temperature beside the menu bar icon, and keeping fans under ChillMac's control when you close the lid while plugged in. Both are off by default, so nothing changes unless you want it to.
## Added
- **Temperature in the menu bar.** Settings, under Display. "When Warm" leaves the menu bar alone until the Mac actually heats up and shows the reading only then, matching the Good / Warm / Hot wording in the main window. "Always" keeps it there the whole time. It follows your °F/°C setting, and stays plain text so it looks right on any wallpaper and in both light and dark menu bars - **Keep Fans When Closed on Power.** Settings, under Fan Control. While on AC, fans stay exactly as ChillMac set them through closing the lid, locking the screen and sleeping, instead of being handed straight back to macOS. Useful for a docked Mac driving an external display. On battery nothing changes, so closing the lid away from a charger still returns the fans to automatic
